name: Color Contrast Checker
description: Check the WCAG contrast ratio between two colors and see whether they pass AA/AAA accessibility thresholds for normal and large text, with a live preview.

faq.question: What contrast ratio do I actually need?
faq.answer: WCAG 2.x AA — 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text (18pt+, or 14pt+ bold), and 3:1 for UI components/graphical objects — is the widely-referenced baseline for accessibility compliance. AAA (7:1 / 4.5:1) is a stricter, optional enhanced level most sites don't fully meet everywhere.

faq.question: How is the ratio calculated?
faq.answer: From each color's WCAG relative luminance (a weighted, gamma-corrected combination of its red/green/blue channels — green contributes far more than blue, matching human perception), then (lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05). Black on white is the maximum possible ratio, 21:1; identical colors are always 1:1.
